summary: imports watch is the public entry's hardened version: polls GET /imports/{id} (no cache) and its launch monitor until completed/failed/cancelled, requires every row counter on the terminal job, and with --verify re-reads the finished job and GET /imports/{id}/side-effects; a failed verification fetch, missing or invalid counters, or side effects that are not complete (queued, failed or held sends) make the result partial and exit 5, as do a failed/cancelled import and the --timeout. Kept from the reprint: --latest, the [jobId] Use line, the --dry-run object; --interval and --timeout take a duration or bare seconds. Two deliberate refinements over the public entry, both seen live on the demo workspace: the job's `errors` field is its issue log (an array), so it is no alias of errorRows; and side effects whose every counter is zero (the route answers isComplete=false for total 0) are reported as no_side_effects and verify, while any queued, retryable, exhausted, failed or held send still fails verification. Round 2 (Codex novel1219-r1): --verify rejects every nonzero queued/retryable/exhausted/failed/held counter and actionRequired regardless of isComplete; the overall deadline is --timeout from the command context (the root request timeout stays per request); a job still running when the loop ends (the dogfood poll cap) is partial, exit 5; the all-zero exception needs a terminal status; typed exits 0,2,3,4,5. Round 3 (Codex novel1219-r2): skippedInactive, pending and processing are read (strict when present) and only completed counts as a successful send: every other nonzero counter, actionRequired, and a completed count below total fail verification (sideEffectCounts / sideEffectProblems).
reason: Greptile round 1 on PR #2450 (P1): the reprint's --verify recorded a failed delivery-report read and still exited 0, and dropped the job-scoped side-effects check.

TestImportsWatchVerifyIsCompleteExactOutput covers the no-side-effects row; TestNovel1219ImportsWatchIgnoresTheJobsIssueLog pins the issue-log case.
